summary: Build practical livestock value chain and animal health management skills in 5 days. Design herd health plans, biosecurity, and risk-based interventions.
lede: Animal health management across livestock value chains coordinates prevention from production through processing for livestock managers and animal-health staff. The course addresses how to identify health risks across the chain and plan responses that support productivity and market access. Participants practice mapping value chains, ranking risks, planning vaccination and deworming schedules, drafting herd health and biosecurity plans, and using basic epidemiological indicators and treatment records.
audienceIntro: You are responsible for keeping animals healthy, products moving, and value chains commercially viable, and you need more than ad hoc treatments to do that well.
audience: Meat or Dairy Plant Quality Assurance Supervisor
modules: Livestock Value Chain Fundamentals and Animal Health Risks
Value Chain Mapping and Health Bottleneck Analysis
Animal Health Management Concepts and Basic Epidemiology
Biosecurity Planning Using OIE and HACCP Principles
Herd Health Plans, Vaccination, and Parasite Control
Digital Records, Treatment Monitoring, and AMR Stewardship
Economic Analysis of Animal Health Interventions
Standards, Certification, and Market Requirements for Animal Health
Integrating Animal Health into Value Chain Governance
Action Planning and Reporting for Livestock Value Chain Health
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course. You should have basic knowledge of livestock production systems (species, production cycles, common diseases) and at least one year of experience in animal husbandry, veterinary services, or livestock marketing. No laboratory work or coding is required. You should be comfortable working with simple spreadsheets for recording herd health data and basic calculations. The course treats value chain analysis and epidemiology at operational application level: you will design and interpret tools and plans, not build complex statistical models. Bringing any existing herd health records, vaccination logs, or value chain project documents from your context is recommended to maximize relevance.
